title: Minimal No-Sorry Package Build Report v0

canonical_node.axiom: A Lean package that builds without sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe under an explicit assumption bundle establishes a conditional kernel, not absolute theological proof.
definitions: No-sorry package: a Lean project that compiles with `lake build` and contains no occurrences of sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in its source files.
Conditional kernel: a set of theorems proven under explicit assumptions (axiom bundle) that are not claimed to be unconditionally true.
Bridge claims: statements that map theological or physical concepts into the formal model but are not proven by the package.
derivation: The package was built with `lake build` and reported 'Build completed successfully.'
A scan with `rg` for sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe found no matches in the Lean source files.
The package contains 7 Lean files and 14 theorem/lemma declarations.
The package proves a conditional kernel: given a World vocabulary and an explicit AxiomBundle, unrestored degradation is incompatible with moral goodness in the model.
The package also proves definitional projections for mercy and grace, and arithmetic facts about a minimal two-factor product model.

The document explicitly states what the package does not prove: God, Christianity, Christ as unique global fixed point, the Lagrangian-to-product bridge, physical law mappings, historical Resurrection, empirical truth of the Master Equation.
canonical_node.action: Treat this package as a verified conditional kernel. Use it as a foundation for further formalization, but do not claim it proves theological or physical truths beyond its explicit assumptions.
boundary: Does not prove God, Christianity, or Christ as unique global fixed point.
Does not prove the Lagrangian-to-product bridge or physical law mappings.
Does not prove historical Resurrection or empirical truth of the Master Equation.
Does not claim that the axiom bundle is consistent or satisfiable without a model.
test: Run `lake build` and confirm 'Build completed successfully.'
Run `rg -n "\b(sorry|admit|axiom|unsafe)\b" minimal_no_sorry_package_draft -g "*.lean" -g "!**/.lake/**"` and confirm no matches.
Verify that the package contains 7 Lean files and 14 theorem/lemma declarations.
Check that public language follows the acceptable phrasing: 'Lean successfully builds a no-sorry minimal Theophysics kernel with 14 theorem/lemma declarations under an explicit assumption bundle.'

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a verified no-sorry conditional kernel for Theophysics, establishing that certain moral statements follow from explicit assumptions, without claiming absolute proof.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the distinction between formal proof under assumptions and empirical/theological truth claims, preventing overstatement.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this node is removed, the verified status of the conditional kernel is lost, and the distinction between formal proof and theological claim becomes unclear.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Preserve as a verified conditional kernel; do not upgrade to absolute proof.

Treating the conditional kernel as unconditional truth.

plain_summary: This document reports that a minimal Lean package builds successfully without sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe, proving a conditional kernel about moral goodness under an explicit axiom bundle. It explicitly disclaims proving God, Christianity, or physical mappings. The node captures this as a verified conditional kernel, not absolute proof.
